Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 1) The most common site of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: About 90–95% of AAAs occur below the renal arteries due to advanced atherosclerosis.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 2) The most common cause of abdominal aortic aneurysm is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Degenerative atherosclerotic disease is the leading cause of infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 3) A pulsatile expansile abdominal mass in an elderly smoker is most suggestive of:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The classical triad is pulsatile abdominal mass, abdominal/back pain and hypotension if rupture occurs.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 4) The investigation of choice for stable abdominal aortic aneurysm is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: CT angiography accurately defines aneurysm size, extent and relation to branch vessels before repair.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 5) The most feared complication of abdominal aortic aneurysm is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Ruptured AAA carries a very high mortality and requires emergency management.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 6) The commonest cause of acute arterial occlusion is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Cardiac emboli, particularly from atrial fibrillation, are the commonest cause of acute limb ischemia.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 7) Acute arterial occlusion classically presents with the “6 Ps” except:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The 6 Ps are Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, Paralysis and Poikilothermia.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 8) The first-line anticoagulant in acute limb ischemia is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Immediate intravenous heparin prevents propagation of thrombus while definitive treatment is arranged.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 9) The commonest source of arterial emboli is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Atrial fibrillation commonly leads to left atrial thrombus formation and systemic embolization.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 10) The investigation of choice before revascularization in peripheral arterial disease is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: CT angiography accurately identifies the site and severity of arterial occlusion.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 11) Intermittent claudication is best described as:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option1: Pain at rest relieved by walking
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option3: Exercise-induced limb pain relieved by rest
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Intermittent claudication is the hallmark symptom of peripheral arterial disease.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 12) The most common cause of peripheral arterial disease is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Atherosclerosis is responsible for the vast majority of chronic lower-limb arterial disease.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 13) Buerger disease is strongly associated with:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Smoking cessation is the single most effective treatment for thromboangiitis obliterans.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 14) The typical patient with Buerger disease is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: It classically affects young heavy smokers and involves small- and medium-sized arteries.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 15) The investigation of choice for suspected deep vein thrombosis is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Duplex Doppler is the first-line imaging modality for diagnosing DVT.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 16) The most common site of deep vein thrombosis is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option2: Calf veins of the lower limb
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Most DVTs originate in the deep veins of the calf and may extend proximally.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 17) The most serious complication of deep vein thrombosis is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Pulmonary embolism is the major life-threatening complication of DVT.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 18) Virchow’s triad includes all except:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Virchow’s triad consists of venous stasis, endothelial injury and hypercoagulability.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 19) The most common cause of varicose veins is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Valve incompetence causes venous reflux and progressive venous dilatation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 20) The investigation of choice for varicose veins is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Duplex Doppler identifies venous reflux, valve incompetence and deep venous patency.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 21) The most common site of primary varicose veins is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The great saphenous vein is most commonly affected because of long-standing venous reflux.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 22) The most common complication of varicose veins is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Chronic venous hypertension may lead to ulceration, especially around the medial malleolus.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 23) Venous ulcers most commonly occur over the:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The gaiter area near the medial malleolus is the characteristic location.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 24) The most common cause of venous ulcer is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Venous valve incompetence causes sustained venous hypertension leading to ulcer formation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 25) The most common organism causing infection in chronic venous ulcers is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest colonizing and infecting organism in chronic leg ulcers.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 26) The Trendelenburg test is used to assess:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: It helps identify incompetence of the saphenofemoral junction and superficial venous valves.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 27) The Perthes test is used to assess:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: A positive Perthes test suggests obstruction of the deep venous system.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 28) The first-line management of uncomplicated varicose veins includes:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Compression therapy relieves symptoms and reduces venous hypertension.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 29) The definitive treatment for symptomatic saphenofemoral junction incompetence is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Modern treatment includes endovenous thermal ablation or surgical ligation with stripping.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 30) The most common cause of secondary varicose veins is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Post-thrombotic syndrome leads to secondary venous valve incompetence.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 31) The investigation of choice for carotid artery stenosis is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Carotid duplex is the preferred initial investigation for suspected carotid stenosis.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 32) The commonest cause of carotid artery stenosis is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Atherosclerotic plaque formation at the carotid bifurcation is the commonest cause.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 33) The most common presentation of carotid artery disease is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Patients often present with transient neurological deficits due to cerebral embolization.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 34) Which of the following is the strongest modifiable risk factor for peripheral arterial disease?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Smoking markedly accelerates atherosclerosis and increases the risk of limb ischemia.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 35) The ankle-brachial index (ABI) is primarily used to diagnose:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: An ABI below 0.9 is diagnostic of peripheral arterial disease.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 36) The most common cause of chronic limb-threatening ischemia is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Advanced peripheral arterial disease is responsible for most cases of chronic limb-threatening ischemia.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 37) Rest pain due to peripheral arterial disease typically:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Lowering the limb improves perfusion and temporarily relieves ischemic rest pain.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 38) Buerger disease primarily affects:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option3: Small- and medium-sized arteries and veins
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Thromboangiitis obliterans is a segmental inflammatory disease of small- and medium-sized vessels.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 39) Which vascular disorder is most strongly associated with migrating superficial thrombophlebitis?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Recurrent migratory superficial thrombophlebitis is a characteristic feature of Buerger disease.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 40) The single most effective treatment for Buerger disease is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Complete cessation of tobacco use is the only intervention proven to halt disease progression.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 41) The most common cause of painless hematuria in an elderly patient is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Painless gross hematuria is the classical presenting symptom of bladder cancer until proven otherwise.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 42) The most common histological type of urinary bladder carcinoma is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: More than 90% of bladder cancers in developed countries are urothelial (transitional cell) carcinomas.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 43) The most important risk factor for urinary bladder carcinoma is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Smoking is the strongest risk factor, accounting for approximately half of bladder cancer cases.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 44) The investigation of choice for suspected bladder carcinoma is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Cystoscopy allows direct visualization and histological confirmation of bladder tumors.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 45) The most common site of renal cell carcinoma is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Renal cell carcinoma arises from the renal tubular epithelium within the renal cortex.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 46) The classical triad of renal cell carcinoma consists of:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option4: Hematuria, loin pain, palpable renal mass
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The classic triad is uncommon but highly suggestive when present.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 47) The investigation of choice for renal cell carcinoma is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Contrast-enhanced CT provides diagnosis, staging and assessment of local extension.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 48) The definitive treatment for localized renal cell carcinoma is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Radical nephrectomy remains the standard treatment for localized operable disease.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 49) The most common site of metastasis from renal cell carcinoma is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The lungs are the most frequent site of distant metastasis in renal cell carcinoma.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 50) The most common type of renal stone is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Calcium oxalate stones account for nearly 70–80% of urinary calculi.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 51) The investigation of choice for suspected urinary tract stone is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Non-contrast CT KUB has the highest sensitivity and specificity for urinary stones.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 52) The most common site of ureteric stone impaction is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The vesicoureteric junction is the narrowest part of the ureter and the commonest site of stone impaction.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 53) A staghorn calculus is most commonly composed of:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Struvite stones are associated with urease-producing bacterial infections.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 54) Which organism is most commonly associated with struvite stones?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Proteus produces urease, increasing urinary pH and promoting magnesium ammonium phosphate stone formation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 55) The commonest symptom of ureteric colic is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option2: Severe colicky loin pain radiating to the groin
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Ureteric obstruction produces intense colicky pain that radiates from the flank to the groin.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 56) The investigation of choice for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option4: Ultrasonography with post-void residual urine assessment
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Ultrasound evaluates prostate size and residual urine volume in patients with LUTS.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 57) The most common symptom of benign prostatic hyperplasia is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Frequency, urgency, nocturia, hesitancy and poor stream are typical features of BPH.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 58) The gold standard surgical treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: TURP remains the standard surgical procedure for moderate to severe symptomatic BPH.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 59) The commonest site of carcinoma of the prostate is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Most prostate cancers arise in the peripheral zone and are detectable on digital rectal examination.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 60) The most useful serum tumor marker for carcinoma of the prostate is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is widely used for diagnosis, risk stratification and follow-up of prostate cancer.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 61) The most common route of spread of carcinoma prostate is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Prostate carcinoma commonly metastasizes to the axial skeleton through the vertebral venous (Batson’s) plexus.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 62) The most common type of bone metastasis in carcinoma prostate is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Prostate cancer classically produces osteoblastic (sclerotic) bone metastases.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 63) The investigation of choice for diagnosing carcinoma prostate is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The diagnosis is confirmed histologically by transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 64) The commonest congenital anomaly of the male external genitalia is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Hypospadias is characterized by a ventral ectopic urethral meatus and is the most common congenital penile anomaly.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 65) Circumcision should be avoided in a child with:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The prepuce may be required for urethral reconstruction during hypospadias repair.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 66) The most common cause of acute scrotal pain in adolescents requiring emergency surgery is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Testicular torsion is a true surgical emergency; prompt detorsion improves testicular salvage.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 67) The investigation of choice for suspected testicular torsion is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Color Doppler demonstrates reduced or absent blood flow. If suspicion is very high, surgery should not be delayed for imaging.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 68) The definitive treatment for testicular torsion is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option2: Emergency surgical exploration with bilateral orchidopexy
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The affected testis is detorsed and fixed, and the contralateral testis is also fixed to prevent future torsion.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 69) The most common cause of painless scrotal swelling that transilluminates is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Hydrocele is a collection of fluid within the tunica vaginalis and typically transilluminates.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 70) A varicocele most commonly occurs on the:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The left internal spermatic vein drains into the left renal vein, making left-sided varicoceles much more common.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 71) The classical description of a varicocele on examination is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Dilated tortuous pampiniform veins produce the characteristic “bag of worms” feel.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 72) A sudden onset right-sided varicocele in an older patient should raise suspicion of:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: A new right-sided varicocele may result from obstruction of the right gonadal vein by a renal malignancy.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 73) The most common malignant tumor of the testis is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Seminoma is the commonest testicular germ cell tumor in adults.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 74) The investigation of choice for a suspected testicular tumor is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Scrotal ultrasound differentiates intratesticular from extratesticular lesions with high accuracy.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 75) The standard initial treatment for testicular cancer is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The inguinal approach avoids tumor seeding of the scrotum and provides definitive diagnosis.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 76) The most common presentation of testicular cancer is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Most patients present with a painless enlarging testicular mass.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 77) Which tumor marker is commonly elevated in seminoma?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Some seminomas produce β-hCG, but AFP should remain normal in pure seminoma.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 78) Which tumor marker is never elevated in pure seminoma?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Elevation of AFP suggests a non-seminomatous germ cell component.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 79) The most common site of metastasis from testicular cancer is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Lymphatic drainage follows the gonadal vessels to the para-aortic nodes.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 80) The investigation of choice for staging testicular cancer is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option3: CT scan of the chest, abdomen and pelvis
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: CT evaluates retroperitoneal lymph nodes and distant metastases, forming the basis of staging.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 81) The most common cause of acute urinary retention in elderly men is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: BPH is the leading cause of acute urinary retention in older men due to bladder outlet obstruction.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 82) The immediate management of acute urinary retention is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Prompt bladder decompression by urethral catheterization is the first-line treatment.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 83) If urethral catheterization fails in acute urinary retention, the next step is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Suprapubic catheterization is indicated when transurethral catheterization is unsuccessful or contraindicated.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 84) The most common cause of urethral stricture is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Pelvic trauma and urethral instrumentation are common causes of urethral stricture disease.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 85) The investigation of choice for urethral stricture is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Retrograde urethrography accurately demonstrates the site and length of the stricture.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 86) The most common symptom of urethral stricture is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Progressive narrowing of the urethra leads to obstructive lower urinary tract symptoms.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 87) The commonest site of injury in pelvic fracture urethral injury is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Posterior urethral injuries usually occur at the bulbomembranous junction after pelvic fractures.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 88) Blood at the external urethral meatus following pelvic trauma indicates:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Urethral injury should be suspected, and urethral catheterization should be avoided until evaluated.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 89) The investigation of choice before catheterization in suspected urethral injury is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Retrograde urethrography confirms urethral integrity before instrumentation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 90) The most common cause of painless enlargement of the scrotum in adults is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Hydrocele presents as a gradually enlarging, painless, fluctuant scrotal swelling.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 91) The investigation of choice for hydrocele is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Ultrasound confirms the diagnosis and excludes an underlying testicular lesion.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 92) The definitive treatment for symptomatic adult hydrocele is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Surgical excision or eversion of the sac is the definitive treatment for symptomatic hydrocele.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 93) The most common cause of epididymitis in sexually active young men is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Chlamydia trachomatis is the leading cause of epididymitis in sexually active men under 35 years.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 94) The most common cause of epididymitis in elderly men is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Gram-negative enteric organisms are the predominant pathogens in older men.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 95) Elevation of the scrotum relieves pain in epididymitis. This is known as:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Pain relief on scrotal elevation favors epididymitis, although it is not completely reliable.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 96) The most common congenital anomaly of testicular descent is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Cryptorchidism is the commonest congenital abnormality affecting testicular position.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 97) The ideal age for orchidopexy in cryptorchidism is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Early orchidopexy improves fertility potential and facilitates surveillance for malignancy.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 98) The greatest long-term risk of an undescended testis is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Cryptorchidism significantly increases the lifetime risk of testicular germ cell tumors.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 99) Which urinary stone is radiolucent on plain X-ray?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Uric acid stones are radiolucent but are readily detected by non-contrast CT.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 100) The most common cause of gross painless hematuria in adults is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Any episode of painless visible hematuria should be considered bladder cancer until proven otherwise.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 101) In an adult, the Parkland formula for fluid resuscitation in burns is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The Parkland formula uses 4 mL of Ringer’s lactate × body weight (kg) × %TBSA burned during the first 24 hours.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 102) According to the Parkland formula, half of the calculated fluid should be given:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option2: In the first 8 hours from the time of burn
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option4: In the first 4 hours from admission
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The timing starts from the moment of injury, not from hospital arrival.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 103) Which fluid is recommended for initial burn resuscitation?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Ringer’s lactate is the preferred crystalloid for initial burn resuscitation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 104) In adults, the Rule of Nines assigns what percentage of TBSA to one entire lower limb?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Each lower limb represents 18% of the total body surface area in adults.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 105) Circumferential full-thickness burns of a limb may require:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Escharotomy relieves vascular compromise caused by the inelastic burn eschar.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 106) The leading cause of death within the first 24 hours after a major burn is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Massive plasma loss causes burn shock during the early post-burn period.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 107) The most reliable indicator of adequate fluid resuscitation in burn patients is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Adults should maintain a urine output of approximately 0.5 mL/kg/hour.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 108) Which burn is characterized by a dry, leathery, painless wound?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Full-thickness burns destroy nerve endings, making the burn painless despite severe tissue injury.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 109) The most common organism causing burn wound infection is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Pseudomonas is the commonest pathogen responsible for burn wound infection.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 110) The indication for tetanus prophylaxis in burn patients is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option1: All significant burns according to immunization status
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Burn wounds are tetanus-prone injuries; prophylaxis depends on vaccination history and wound severity.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 111) Healing by primary intention occurs in:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option2: Clean surgical incisions with wound edges approximated
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Primary intention results in rapid healing with minimal scar formation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 112) The strongest tissue in the body during wound healing is formed during the:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Collagen remodeling increases tensile strength over months, although wounds never regain 100% strength.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 113) Which vitamin is essential for collagen synthesis and wound healing?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Vitamin C is required for hydroxylation of collagen and normal wound repair.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 114) Which mineral deficiency delays wound healing?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Zinc is essential for DNA synthesis, cell proliferation and wound repair.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 115) The most common organism causing surgical site infection is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Staphylococcus aureus remains the leading pathogen in postoperative wound infections.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 116) The gold standard treatment of an abscess is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Antibiotics alone rarely cure an abscess because pus prevents adequate antibiotic penetration.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 117) The most common complication of untreated wound infection is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Infection weakens wound healing and predisposes to separation of wound edges.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 118) Which suture material is absorbable ?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Vicryl is a synthetic absorbable braided suture commonly used for soft tissue approximation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 119) Which suture material is non-absorbable ?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Prolene is a monofilament, non-absorbable suture with excellent tensile strength.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 120) Which drain works by negative suction ?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Jackson-Pratt is a closed suction drain that reduces dead space and lowers infection risk.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 121) The most important principle in the management of hemorrhagic shock is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option1: Early control of bleeding and fluid resuscitation
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option4: Immediate blood transfusion for all patients
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Rapid hemorrhage control with appropriate fluid and blood replacement is the cornerstone of treatment.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 122) The earliest clinical sign of hypovolemic shock is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Tachycardia is an early compensatory response to reduced circulating blood volume.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 123) Which crystalloid solution is preferred for the initial management of hemorrhagic shock?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Balanced crystalloids such as Ringer’s lactate are recommended for initial fluid resuscitation.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 124) Which of the following is the universal donor for packed red blood cells?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: O-negative red blood cells can be transfused in emergencies when blood grouping is unavailable.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 125) Which blood group is the universal recipient for red blood cell transfusion?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: AB-positive individuals can receive red blood cells from all ABO and Rh blood groups.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 126) The most common immediate complication of blood transfusion is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: This is the commonest acute transfusion reaction and presents with fever and chills.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 127) The most serious acute transfusion reaction is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: ABO incompatibility can rapidly lead to shock, DIC, acute kidney injury and death.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 128) The first step in managing a suspected transfusion reaction is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: The transfusion must be stopped immediately while maintaining IV access with normal saline and investigating the reaction.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 129) The most common cause of septic shock in surgical patients is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Gram-negative organisms remain a major cause of septic shock in surgical practice.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 130) The cornerstone of treatment of septic shock includes:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option3: Early broad-spectrum antibiotics with aggressive fluid resuscitation
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Early recognition, prompt antibiotics, adequate fluid resuscitation and source control significantly improve survival.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 131) Which electrolyte disturbance is most commonly associated with prolonged vomiting?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Loss of gastric hydrochloric acid leads to metabolic alkalosis, while potassium depletion causes hypokalemia.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 132) Which electrolyte disturbance is commonly seen in prolonged diarrhea?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Loss of bicarbonate-rich intestinal fluid causes metabolic acidosis.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 133) The most common electrolyte abnormality after prolonged nasogastric suction is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Continuous gastric drainage results in loss of hydrochloric acid and chloride.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 134) Which electrolyte abnormality is most likely to produce cardiac arrhythmias?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Hypokalemia predisposes to ventricular arrhythmias and characteristic ECG changes.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 135) The preferred route of nutritional support in a patient with a functioning gastrointestinal tract is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: “If the gut works, use it.” Enteral feeding preserves gut integrity and reduces infectious complications.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 136) Total parenteral nutrition is indicated when:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option1: The patient is tolerating oral feeding
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option3: The gastrointestinal tract is functioning normally
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option4: Enteral feeding is impossible or contraindicated
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: TPN is reserved for patients in whom adequate enteral nutrition cannot be provided.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 137) The most common metabolic complication of total parenteral nutrition is:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Frequent glucose monitoring is essential during TPN to detect and manage hyperglycemia.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 138) Which phase of wound healing is characterized by fibroblast proliferation and collagen deposition?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Fibroblasts, angiogenesis and granulation tissue formation occur predominantly during the proliferative phase.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 139) Keloids characteristically:
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option1: Extend beyond the boundaries of the original wound
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.option2: Remain confined to the original wound
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: Unlike hypertrophic scars, keloids grow beyond the original wound margins and have a high recurrence rate.

Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.question: 140) Which of the following is an example of a clean surgical wound ?
Vascular Surgery, Urology, Miscellaneous.exp: A clean wound is an uninfected operative wound in which no inflammation or entry into contaminated viscera occurs.
